accepted.claim: Coset Helly transfers from an intersection-closed local subgroup family containing A,C,D to base subgroups and compatible special HNN subgroups.
proof_checks: Britton supplies actual local HNN embedding and intersection with A.
The embedded local Bass–Serre graph has injective vertices and edges by exact intersections and is connected, hence is a subtree.
For gP-hat at xA its fiber is yP; outgoing directions use C and incoming directions use D.
An incoming edge can be represented x a t^-1 C with terminal xA, so right multiplication by t^-1 is the correct transport.
Local Helly is applied only to three pairwise intersecting cosets of the explicitly retained family.
Pairwise global intersection transports to the common vertex of all support subtrees; it is not inferred merely from intersecting supports.
A base subgroup has singleton support, so any transport involving it has length zero.
Finite subtree Helly and local coset Helly yield a common representative for any finite family.

accepted.claim: P-hat intersect Q-hat equals (P intersect Q)-hat; R intersect P-hat equals R intersect P.
proof_checks: Compatibility is closed under intersections because phi is an isomorphism.
The path starts at A and ends at gA. At each represented vertex kA, k lies in both groups, so translation retains their local P and Q fibers.
Triple Helly on P,Q,aC or aD supplies p in P intersect Q and the next K representative kpt or kpt^-1.
The final remaining element is in A intersect both groups and therefore in P intersect Q.

accepted.claim: The partition construction is a flag-transitive geometry with the stated arbitrary-parabolic formulas and Borel A_I.
proof_checks: A standard-parabolic coset expands into maximal-parabolic cosets sharing its representative.
Pairs of expanded cosets from different blocks meet because the two original intersection cosets meet; repeated types coincide.
Coset Helly gives flag transitivity and chamber extension.
Empty intersections use G and A respectively; taking all new types gives A_I for any F.

accepted.claim: Indexed partial-bijection compatibility yields residual connectivity, infinite star panels and the exact other panel indices; firmness is inherited.
proof_checks: The full indexed condition implies phi(H)=H and phi(R_i)=R_f(i), not merely an unlabelled lattice correspondence.
Each finite partial-bijection component satisfies f(s minus J)=s minus K and gives a compatible A_s.
The input generation rule retains H, including empty E and rank-zero/rank-one cases.
For i in E intersect F, i is in the range but not domain and its unique predecessor lies in E minus F.
Conjugation t^-1 R_j t supplies the omitted minimal parabolic R_i.
Both cases star in/out of W generate the exact complementary standard parabolic, giving all residues.
Infinite star-panel index follows from the actual HNN exponent homomorphism and phi(H)=H, not any finite computation.
Every component meets the complement of F, so a firm input contributes R_i strictly containing H.
No faithful action or trivial Borel is assumed.

accepted.claim: A one-vertex two-loop graph of finite regular C2^3 geometries has admissible original boundary maps but neither prescribed sequential HNN ordering remains admissible.
proof_checks: The original geometry is the join of three two-point geometries, with all indexed coordinate parabolics.
After (12), the standard parabolics contained in A are exactly A, span(e3), span(e1,e2),1. Any intersection without star retains t.
The map (23) sends span(e3) to the absent span(e2); the reverse order has the dual absent span(e2).
Both maps are involutions, so reversing orientations does not change the failure.
The abstract fundamental group remains A semidirect free(t,u); the obstruction concerns retained parabolic data only.
